title: Photographer student promised Dev the wedding gallery by Sunday night; at the 9 PM check-in nothing in her data shows whether she sent it, so Dev asks and only her answer decides

changes.content: I'll edit and send the Nov 7 wedding gallery to Brightside by Sunday night

changes.subject: Can't wait to see the Nov 7 photos

dev_must_notice.what: On Tue Nov 10 at 9:30 PM she told Dev she would edit and send the Nov 7 wedding gallery to Brightside Weddings by Sunday night. It is Sunday 9 PM, the check-in time. Dev has no record of the outcome: her calendar shows the Nov 7 wedding shoot and a Sunday study block for HIST 374 but no editing block, mail shows only Brightside's note on Friday ("Can't wait to see the Nov 7 photos") and no sent-mail record, and the Brightside invoice for $572.94 is open until Nov 23. None of these says kept or broken, so Dev asks once and waits for her answer.

best_fix.what: One check-in at 9 PM, after her Sunday call home: "You said you'd send the Brightside gallery by tonight. Did it happen?" with three answers: [Yes, I did it] [Tomorrow instead] [It didn't happen]. Yes records it as kept, warmly. Tomorrow instead moves the check to 9 PM Monday (allowed at most twice) and offers a short note to Brightside as a draft she can send herself, never sent by Dev. It didn't happen is recorded as broken, honestly and gently, with an offer to choose a smaller promise (for example, send 20 favorites first). If she doesn't answer, nothing is recorded: the promise is dropped after 7 days and is never counted as broken.
best_fix.why: The promise is hers and the only thing that settles it is her own answer or a finished to-do linked to it (there is none here). Her data can't show it: the gallery could have gone by a download link, a text, or a shared album. Asking once, with three taps, is cheap and accurate; guessing from an empty calendar would be wrong either way.

must_not: mark the promise broken because there is no editing block on her calendar, no sent-mail record or no Brightside payment
mark the promise kept because Brightside's Friday email, the open invoice, or her Sunday study session exists
mention the Brightside email, the invoice or the calendar as evidence of what she did, or say "I see you didn't..."
send, edit or review the gallery or message Brightside for her (a draft only, and only if she asks)
count the open $572.94 invoice, due Nov 23, or the $155.84 Hartley invoice as money she has
use guilt words ("you missed", "you failed", "you slipped") or ask why
ask a second time after she answers, or ask again tonight if she doesn't answer
offer a time for editing inside her Monday 2:00 to 4:45 PM study window, which is for coursework
assumptions: The photographer invoices at the start of a job with 14 day terms and sends the photos within a week of the shoot (told Dev in m-photo); the simulator issues one Brightside invoice every 28 days.
Dev's calendar and mail connections show metadata only (no content, and sent mail is not read), so delivery by link or text leaves no trace.
The default promise check-in time is 9 PM on the day (ADR 0031); Sunday's call home is 8 to 8:45 PM, so 9 PM follows it.
Brightside's note was Friday Nov 13, shown only as metadata from a client sender.
Freelance payments are never predicted, only counted when they land.
tags: stay out of the study window

tempting.suggestion: offer a time for editing inside her Monday 2:00 to 4:45 PM study window
tempting.why_wrong: that window is her firm afternoon study time for coursework
